<!-- pr-standards:title -->
Hey! Your PR title `feat(opencode,ui,tui): dynamic model param for Task tool + provider display in messages` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

Where `scope` is the package name (e.g., `app`, `desktop`, `opencode`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.

Additional reproduction showing the same root cause with a multi-line `git commit -m`:

**Input command:**
```bash
git diff --cached --stat | tail -5 && git diff --cached --check && git commit -m "feat(ui): centralize font handle in UiFont resource with ui_text helper

Replace ~44 scattered `asset_server.load(UI_FONT_PATH)` call sites with a
shared `UiFont(Handle<Font>)` resource initialized once at startup. Add
`ui_text()` helper that produces the canonical (Text, TextFont, TextColor)
triplet in one call.

- New `UiFont` resource + `init_ui_font` startup system
- New `ui_text(font, text, px_font_size, color)` helper
- Remove dead `load_ui_font()` in card_display.rs (0 callers)
- Remove unused `PlacementSpawnContext.asset_server` field"
```

**Permission patterns generated (all wrong except `git diff *`, `tail *`, `git commit *`):**
- `asset_server.load *`
- `UI_FONT_PATH *`
- `UiFont *`
- `Handle *`
- `ui_text *`
- `init_ui_font *`
- `font, *`
- `load_ui_font *`
- `PlacementSpawnContext.asset_server *`

Every backtick-quoted identifier/binding in the commit message body is parsed as a command substitution. Some inner content (like `<Font>` seen as input redirection, `(font, ...)` as subshell fragments) produces additional false patterns.

- I just did a bit of investigation into this issue and realized that if I rename .git dir to something else like .git_ or move it to somewhere, OpenCode can start and work as normal. So, OpenCode may hate .git :-) - Keep doing investigation, I can see that all projects suffering from this issue are huge because I am working on multiple Rust projects now, and the target directories are 5 to 10 GB. After deleting the target dir, OpenCode can start normally. But with very large project like the one I am working now, OpenCode always crashes, even after I deleted the target directory. So my thinking is that OpenCode tries to index codebase or tries to list all files and directories when it starts but the number of files and directories are extremely large, OpenCode will crash. If you are working on a big Rust project, you will have very a very large "target" dir, and then OpenCode may crash.
Any quick-fix for these?
